rationale: Evidence: iteration 7 (base_speed 1.1, kp 4.5, ki 0.02, kd 1.0, 5 sensors at y 0.08 with x spread ±0.05, sensor_size 0.016, wheel_track 0.12, mass 0.5, body_length 0.12) finished 60/60 trials with a score of 929.76, the best so far. Oval, s-bend and slalom all completed 20/20 at 2.39, 2.44 and 2.63 s. Iteration 8 raised base_speed to 1.2 and the slalom fell to 18/20 with 2 off-track exits (score 908), so 1.2 is past the safe limit. Iteration 6 at speed 1.0 scored 929.37, so the speed gain between them is small. The score is close to its ceiling for this design: about 500 for completion, 250 for progress, about 105 from one line-loss event, about 65 from rms_error (about 0.011), and about 12 from time. Change: none to the design. I resubmit iteration 7 unchanged, because it is the best verified candidate and the one remaining lever (speed) is shown to be unsafe above 1.1. Expected result: about 930 with all tracks finishing and slalom max_error near 0.023, well inside the 0.06 m off-track limit. Hypotheses for next iteration, not acted on now: (1) the single line-loss event per run probably happens at the start or finish when the sensors leave the tape, so gains may not remove it; (2) the s-bend rms_error (0.016) is the largest tracking term, and a small kd increase might reduce it if oscillation stays low. Measurements requested: completion, progress and completion_time to confirm the design is unchanged in performance; line_loss_events; max_error and steering_oscillation for slalom margin; rms_error for the s-bend term; controller_errors to confirm no exceptions.
